question_variants.resolution_summary: The material is defined as consisting of five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios, but no specific tolerance range or numerical definition of 'near-equal' is provided.

answers.answer: High-entropy nanoalloys (HENA) are defined as nanostructures composed of five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
evidence_spans: To extend the potential of nanoalloys in different fields such as catalysis or mechanics, much attention has recently been paid to multi‐element nanoparticles (NPs), also known as high‐entropy nanoalloys (HENA), which consist of nanostructures composed of five or more metals, in equal or near‐equal atomic ratios, crystallized in a solid solution.
